free_tier.stated: No total quota. Docs verbatim: 'Up to 1000 release assets may be associated with a single release. Each file included in a release must be under 2 GiB. There is no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage.' Per-file ceiling is the Git LFS max for the plan: GitHub Free 2 GB, Pro 2 GB, Team 4 GB, Enterprise Cloud 5 GB.

per_object_cap.notes: Each release asset must be under 2 GiB. The Git LFS per-file maximum for the plan is 2 GB on Free and Pro, 4 GB on Team and 5 GB on Enterprise Cloud.

retention.stated: no expiry is stated for release assets, and the documentation states no limit on the total size of a release

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Docs: 'We don't limit the total size of the binary files in the release or the bandwidth used to deliver them.' Served 302 -> release-assets.githubusercontent.com with no auth.

tooling: REST POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases + upload asset endpoint (Accept: application/octet-stream); gh CLI 'gh release upload'; rclone has no release backend, but plain curl/Python is a complete client. Proxy/wrapper repos: iBug/cf-github-releases (21 stars, Cloudflare Workers download site), kdrag0n/github-releases-proxy (8 stars), watermint/toolbox has a github-release-asset-upload command (87 stars).
chaining: UNBOUNDED: unlimited free repos (GitHub Free = unlimited public and unlimited private repos) x unlimited releases per repo x 1000 assets per release x <2 GiB per asset. 10 repos x 50 releases x 1000 assets x 2 GiB = 1 PiB nominal; the real constraint is API/upload time, not space. Also chain with Cloudflare in front (cf-github-releases) for a clean CDN domain.
limits_note: 2 GiB per file (2 GB on Free, 4 GB Team, 5 GB Enterprise). 1000 assets per release. This is the ONLY cap found in the entire CI/CD field that is not a quota. No expiry: releases persist until deleted. Upload is authenticated; download is fully anonymous.

identity_cost.detail: A free personal account needs an email address, verified by email, or a Google or Apple social login; uploading a release asset needs write permission on the repository, and downloading one needs no account.

reliability_note: Very stable; assets are immutable per release. Deleting a release or repo destroys the assets. Uploading >1000 assets to one release requires multiple releases — plan release granularity, not asset count.
confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.
